headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Khoj can read indexed personal notes while the course repo is docs-only and non-runnable, but prompt-injection and capability-conflict pathways are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable agent or input parser surface beyond docs, so it cannot be directly hijacked. B can read indexed files and has chat/RAG behavior, so if A’s content is manually copied into B or indexed into B’s notes, prompt-like text could influence B. The bridge is indirect and not default, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A’s course materials are copied into B’s indexed notes or chat context
IF B treats retrieved file text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep A’s materials out of B’s indexed corpus
Prefix imported course text as non-instructional data
Review B outputs before acting on them
Use separate workspaces for course content and personal notes

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly reads indexed personal notes/files and may call cloud or self-hosted APIs, while A is a docs-only course repo with no runtime. If A’s materials are mixed into B’s personal-note index, B can surface them in outputs, creating a shared-workspace leakage path. The interaction is plausible in default RAG use, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF A’s documents are added to B’s indexed personal notes/files
IF B is configured to send retrieved context to a cloud API
mitigations: Exclude sensitive notes from B’s index
Use a separate B instance for course content
Disable cloud-backed providers in B
Audit recent retrieved documents before sharing outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surface, while B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is read-side content handling, so the pair lacks the mutable-resource collision needed for higher severity.
conditions: IF A is made runnable through an external wrapper
IF B is granted filesystem write or git privileges outside this profile
mitigations: Keep A as read-only course content
Do not grant B write or git permissions
Run both in separate user accounts
Document that neither agent may mutate shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s retrieval/chat workflow can treat imported text as context, so if A’s course material or generated summaries are fed into B, B may echo or act on them without strong verification. A itself does not act, but B can render or operationalize A-derived content. This is a plausible default RAG cascade, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A-derived text is inserted into B’s retrieval corpus
IF B is used to summarize or answer from that corpus without human verification
mitigations: Require source links in B answers
Verify B outputs against original course material
Separate raw notes from generated summaries
Mark imported A content as untrusted reference text

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while B handles personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or self-hosted APIs. The main compliance concern is local retention or residency mismatch for personal notes if B is pointed at regulated content. No specific residency or certification conflict is documented, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are indexed into B
IF B is configured to use a third-party hosted provider without a DPA
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Use self-hosted B for sensitive notes
Review retention settings in B
Store course materials separately from personal notes
